paper.title: Exponential Regret Bounds for Gaussian Process Bandits with Deterministic Observations

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian process bandits with deterministic observations
unmapped: objective f is a sample path of a zero-mean GP prior with known kernel hyperparameters; function values observed exactly (noise-free)
learner samples from a fixed finite lattice L in D
settings.definition_quote: As in (Srinivas et al., 2010), the objective function is distributed according to a Gaussian process prior: f(x) ~ GP(m(.), kappa(.,.)). ... our assumption is that once the function has been probed at point x in D, then the value f(x) can be observed with very high precision.

algorithms.name: Branch and Bound (GP-UCB with search-space shrinking)

symbols.tau: positive decay constant depending on behaviour of f near its maximum
symbols.T_0: integer threshold T after which the bound holds
symbols.alpha_conf: failure probability alpha in (0,1) used by the algorithm

conditions: kernel four times differentiable along the diagonal
f ~ GP(0,kappa) continuous sample with unique global maximum x_M
either (dagger) x_M interior with quadratic upper/lower bounds near x_M on ball B(x_M, rho_0), or (double dagger) x_M on boundary, f and boundary smooth at x_M with nonzero gradient
lattice L satisfies 2L ∩ conv(L) ⊆ L and is fine enough (condition (5)) in case (dagger)

source.quote: Then, there exist positive numbers A and τ and an integer T such that the points specified by the Branch and Bound algorithm, {x_t}, will satisfy the following asymptotic bound: For all t > T, with probability 1 − α we have r(x_t) < A e^{−τt/(ln t)^{d/4}}.

results.notes: Bound is on instantaneous regret r(x_t) = f(x_M) - f(x_t) of the point sampled at round t, hence quantity 'other'. Probability 1-alpha is over GP prior. Paper's alpha (confidence) renamed alpha_conf.

source.quote: Given κ, f ∼ GP(0, κ) and L ⊆ D as in Theorem 2, the cumulative regret is bounded from above.

results.notes: Corollary only states boundedness (constant in T) of cumulative regret; probability type implied by Theorem 2 (w.p. 1-alpha) but not explicitly stated.
